en: The morning bell, the evening drum
where: 老刘 at the teahouse gives it to you after you meet the stone lion (chapter 1).

pages.zh: 很多年前，北京人没有手机。那他们怎么知道几点了？
pages.en: Many years ago the people of Beijing had no phones. So how did they know what time it was?

pages.zh: 听！鼓楼上有鼓，钟楼上有钟。鼓楼在南边，钟楼在北边。
pages.en: Listen! On the Drum Tower there are drums, on the Bell Tower there is a bell. The Drum Tower is to the south, the Bell Tower to the north.

pages.zh: 晚上七点，鼓楼打鼓。打完鼓，钟楼再敲钟。这时候，城门都不开了。
pages.en: At seven in the evening the Drum Tower beat its drum. When the drum had finished, the Bell Tower rang its bell. From then on the city gates stayed shut.

pages.zh: 夜里，钟两个小时敲一次。早上很早的时候，也是打完鼓，再敲钟。
pages.en: In the night the bell rang once every two hours. Very early in the morning, too, the drum came first, and then the bell.

pages.zh: 一次打多少下？快的十八下，慢的十八下，不快不慢的十八下，再来一次：一百零八下！
pages.en: How many strokes each time? Eighteen fast, eighteen slow, eighteen neither fast nor slow, and all of it once more: a hundred and eight!

pages.zh: 很多年前，鼓楼有二十五个鼓：一个大鼓是一年，二十四个小鼓是二十四个节气。
pages.en: Many years ago the Drum Tower had twenty-five drums: one big drum for the year, and twenty-four small drums for the twenty-four 节气.

pages.zh: 钟楼的钟非常大，有六十三吨。很远的家里也能听见它。
pages.en: The Bell Tower's bell is enormous: sixty-three tonnes. Even homes far away could hear it.

pages.zh: 所以人们说“晨钟暮鼓”：早上的钟，晚上的鼓。
pages.en: That is why people say 晨钟暮鼓: the bell of the morning, the drum of the evening.

today.zh: 今天的北京：白天，鼓楼上一天打好几次鼓。你可以上去听听。钟楼的大钟也还在。
today.en: In Beijing today: in the daytime the drums on the Drum Tower are played several times a day. You can go up and listen. The Bell Tower's big bell is still there too.

words.en: the 24 solar terms of the farmer's year

where: 王阿姨 gives it to you when the old lantern breaks (chapter 1).

pages.zh: 这是一本书，说的是灯笼。中国人很喜欢灯笼。过年的时候，很多家门口都有灯笼。
pages.en: This is a book about lanterns. Chinese people love lanterns. At New Year, many front doors have lanterns.

pages.zh: 灯笼里面有一个小灯。晚上，灯笼很好看。
pages.en: Inside a lantern there is a little light. In the evening the lanterns look lovely.

pages.zh: 有一个灯笼叫走马灯。点上灯，它就自己转起来了。
pages.en: There is a lantern called a 走马灯. Light it, and it starts to turn all by itself.

pages.zh: 为什么会转？下面的灯很热，热热的东西往上走，上面的小东西就转了。
pages.en: Why does it turn? The light at the bottom is hot; the warmth goes up, and the little thing at the top turns.

pages.zh: 走马灯上有很多小画。灯一转，画里的人就走起来了，跑起来了。
pages.en: On a 走马灯 there are many little pictures. When the lantern turns, the people in the pictures start to walk, and run.

pages.zh: 过年了，第十五天是元宵节。这天晚上，大家都出去看灯，还猜灯谜。
pages.en: The New Year comes, and its fifteenth day is 元宵节. That evening everyone goes out to look at the lanterns, and guesses 灯谜.

pages.zh: 灯谜是写在灯笼上的问题。你猜对了，就很高兴！
pages.en: A 灯谜 is a question written on a lantern. If you guess it right, you are very happy!

today.zh: 今天的北京：元宵节的晚上，北京有很多很多灯。有的灯上还有灯谜。你也可以去看看，猜一猜！
today.en: In Beijing today: on the evening of 元宵节 Beijing has lanterns and lanterns and lanterns. Some of them even have riddles. You can go and look too, and have a guess!

words.en: a turning lantern — its pictures seem to run
a riddle written on a lantern

where: 赵爷爷 on 南锣鼓巷 gives it to you when you ask the way to the 鼓楼 (chapter 1).

pages.zh: 北京有很多石狮子。它们在大门口，左边一个，右边一个。
pages.en: Beijing has many stone lions. They stand at big gates, one on the left and one on the right.

pages.zh: 石狮子都是两个一起的：一个是狮子爸爸，一个是狮子妈妈。
pages.en: Stone lions always come two together: one is the father lion, one is the mother lion.

pages.zh: 怎么知道哪个是爸爸？狮子爸爸的脚下有一个球。狮子妈妈的脚下有一个小狮子。
pages.en: How do you know which is the father? Under the father lion's paw there is a ball. Under the mother lion's paw there is a little lion.

pages.zh: 你在门里，往外看：左边的是爸爸，右边的是妈妈。
pages.en: Stand inside the gate and look out: the one on the left is the father, the one on the right is the mother.

pages.zh: 你从外面走到门口，看到的是：右边的是爸爸，左边的是妈妈。
pages.en: Walk up to the gate from outside, and what you see is: the one on the right is the father, the one on the left is the mother.

pages.zh: 门口为什么有狮子？人们说，有狮子在门口，坏人就不来了。它们看着门，也看着家里的人。
pages.en: Why are there lions at gates? People say that with lions at the gate, bad people stay away. They watch the gate, and they watch over the people of the house too.

pages.zh: 有人说，很多很多年前，鼓楼前面也有两个铁狮子。现在没有了。
pages.en: Some say that many, many years ago there were two iron lions in front of the 鼓楼 as well. Now they are gone.

today.zh: 今天的北京：天安门前面有石狮子。故宫的太和门前面，有两个很大的狮子。你去看看：哪个是爸爸？
today.en: In Beijing today: there are stone lions in front of 天安门. In front of the palace's 太和门 there are two very big lions. Go and look: which one is the father?
